subject: Taxes
title: Post-Soviet Tax Distrust
description: A 60-second lesson on Post-Soviet Tax Distrust.

hook.text: After the USSR collapsed, Russia introduced income tax.

buildup.text: Soviet citizens didn't file returns. Taxes were deducted automatically by the state.

discovery.text: Russia adopted a flat 13% income tax in 2001. Simplicity worked.

twist.text: But corporate evasion exploded. Oligarchs used offshore structures to avoid billions.

climax.text: Building tax culture from scratch takes generations.

punchline.text: 13% flat tax, simple and effective. But trust takes generations to build.

quiz.question: Why did Russia's flat 13% income tax succeed at increasing revenue?
options: It was the highest rate in the world
Its simplicity made it understandable and acceptable to citizens
The penalty for evasion was extremely harsh
